How many tickets cover the cost of one workshop?

Add the costs you pay even if nobody books, such as room hire and the instructor’s fee. Subtract the materials used by one guest from one ticket’s price. Divide your fixed costs by that amount and round up to a whole seat. Compare that number with the room’s capacity before you publish tickets.

Sell workshop seats on Shopify →

Worked example

A ceramics studio pays $240 for the room and instructor. Each $45 ticket uses $5 of clay, leaving $40 toward the fixed costs. Six seats cover the session. With ten paid guests, the studio has $160 left after the costs it entered.

Common questions

Where should I put the instructor’s pay?

A flat fee for running the class goes into fixed costs. If the instructor earns a fee for every student who attends, include that amount in the cost per participant.

What if the break-even attendance exceeds my capacity?

At your current ticket price, even a sold-out session would leave a shortfall. Try a different ticket price, a less expensive room or a lower materials cost to see which change makes the class viable.
